text:
olivia (Customer): hey - we're seeing users hit a redirect loop after OAuth with both Google and GitHub. they complete provider login, get redirected back to our /auth/callback but then the app immediately sends them back to the provider. no obvious error shown to user, just loops. started after a deploy yesterday. any ideas? :confused:

alice (Support): sorry about that — can you paste the exact redirect URL you see in the browser when the loop happens? is state present in the querystring?

olivia (Customer): yep here's the URL we see after provider redirect: `https://app.customer.example.com/auth/callback?code=4/0AX4XfWH...&state=YXNkd...` then browser goes to `/login` then back to provider. we use PKCE. github + google both behave same for some users, but other users succeed. incognito sometimes works.

matt (SRE): incognito sometimes works -> sounds like a cookie/session issue. possible that the session cookie storing the `state` or `code_verifier` is not being set or sent on the callback. are you using SameSite cookies? anything changed in the last deploy related to auth cookies or our proxy?

olivia (Customer): we set session cookie as `session_id` with `SameSite=Lax; Secure` and domain `.customer.example.com`. app is behind our LB which does TLS termination; callback path is `/auth/callback` on the app. deploy included an nginx upgrade.

alice (Support): Lax can block cookies for cross-site POSTs depending on how provider redirects. callback is a cross-site GET with query params — Lax normally allows top-level GET navigations, but browsers have tightened rules. try `SameSite=None; Secure` for the session cookie as a quick test. also confirm cookie domain exactly matches (no stray port, and leading dot vs no leading dot can matter for some clients).

sara (Eng): another common cause: our LB/nginx might be rewriting or normalizing the redirect_uri that we registered with the provider. if the redirect_uri the provider calls doesn't exactly match the one registered in the OAuth app (including trailing slash), we sometimes drop `state` validation or treat it as mismatch. can you paste the OAuth app redirect_uris from provider settings?

olivia (Customer): Google has `https://app.customer.example.com/auth/callback` (no trailing slash). GitHub the same. our app sometimes receives `https://app.customer.example.com/auth/callback/` (extra slash) in the referrer after the nginx upgrade. could that cause a mismatch?

matt (SRE): yes — providers compare exact strings when validating redirect_uri during the token exchange flow. But more importantly, the state/PKCE check happens in our app after provider redirects. if our session store keys are computed based on the normalized URL or if the LB strips/rewrites `Cookie` headers for certain paths, session lookup may fail -> we then treat the callback as invalid and re-initiate the auth flow, causing the loop.

alice (Support): can you paste a minimal server log around the time of the callback? look for `state` lookup failures or `code_verifier` mismatch logs. if none, add logging for those checks.

olivia (Customer): here's a snippet from our logs (redacted):

```
2026-02-18T15:02:41Z INFO  auth: received callback, provider=google, query={code: '4/0AX4Xf...', state: 'YXNkd...'}
2026-02-18T15:02:41Z WARN  auth: session lookup failed for session_id=null
2026-02-18T15:02:41Z INFO  auth: initiating oauth redirect to https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth?client_id=...&state=YXNkd...
```

matt (SRE): session_id=null -> cookie wasn't sent. check Set-Cookie response on the initial /login redirect. If LB sets `SameSite` or strips `Set-Cookie` for third-party contexts, that could explain per-user differences. Also, browsers blocking third-party cookies on cross-site SSO flows is common.

olivia (Customer): i checked via devtools: on first redirect to provider we do `302 -> https://accounts.google.com/...` with response header `Set-Cookie: session_id=abc123; Path=/; SameSite=Lax; Secure; HttpOnly`. the browser seems to store it, but on the provider redirect back we don't see the cookie included in the request to `/auth/callback`. some users on Chrome stable see cookie omitted, others have it.

sara (Eng): Chrome has been rolling changes. For cross-site navigations that involve intermediate redirects, Lax may not be enough. Try `SameSite=None; Secure` plus ensure Secure flag set. Also check whether `domain` attribute is present and correct.

raj (Security): also verify PKCE handling: we store `code_verifier` server-side tied to the session. if session isn't preserved, code_verifier is lost and we reject exchange. alternative is to support stateless PKCE by encoding a short-lived `nonce` in the state param that includes HMAC of code_challenge, but that's a larger change. For immediate mitigation, ensure cookies survive the round-trip or fall back to a server-side persistent store keyed to the user's IP or a short-lived cache (careful with security).

alice (Support): can you reproduce locally with `curl` simulating the callback while omitting the `Cookie` header? Eg: `curl -v "https://app.customer.example.com/auth/callback?code=...&state=..."` and inspect server behavior. If it redirects to provider again, you have a deterministic repro.

olivia (Customer): i reproduced: without Cookie header server responds 302 -> /login which then redirects to provider. with Cookie header present it exchanges code for token and completes. so we confirmed cookie missing = loop.

matt (SRE): next steps: 1) temporary config change to `SameSite=None; Secure` and deploy to a small subset, monitor success rate. 2) add defensive check to avoid immediate re-initiation of full OAuth if callback arrives without session: show an error page instructing users to clear cookies or a link to start login again, rather than auto-redirecting (prevents infinite loop). 3) confirm no proxy strips `Cookie` for callback path.

sara (Eng): small note: ensure you don't set `SameSite=None` without `Secure` (browsers will ignore it). also double-check that you're not accidentally setting multiple `Set-Cookie` headers with different attributes; nginx upgrades sometimes changed how we pass Set-Cookie through.

olivia (Customer): thanks — changing to `SameSite=None; Secure` in a canary fixed it for the failing users within 10 minutes. i'll keep canary running and open a deploy PR to roll this change.

alice (Support): great. i'll document this in the support KB: oauth callbacks + nginx upgrade -> check SameSite and redirect_uri normalization. adding ticket to security for review of PKCE fallback options. :white_check_mark:

oauth-bot: created ticket IN-7892 for escalation to Security team (raj) and Eng (sara).

raj (Security): will review IN-7892 tomorrow, but happy with the mitigation. Long term we should consider making the callback flow more tolerant: explicit error page when state missing, better telemetry for callback failures (counts by provider, percent that re-initiate), and a hardened PKCE fallback design.

olivia (Customer): awesome, thanks everyone. will report back after full rollout. :pray:
